Boros · +1/+1 counters army + planeswalkers · Bracket 4 and 3

Lae’zel counters army

Lae’zel with Guild Artisan as her Background. Tested on Kevin’s homelab across 1,800 random four-player tables per version (4,368 games at bracket 4, 4,407 at bracket 3). Point at any card name to see the card.

40.3%Games won, bracket 4
36.2%Series won, bracket 4
38.3%Games won, bracket 3
33.3%Series won, bracket 3
34.9%Knocked out first (B4)
12.3Average rounds per game

How it wins

Lae’zel adds one to every counter you put on a creature or planeswalker. The deck goes wide with creatures and tokens and lets that +1 snowball: Cathars' Crusade, Felidar Retreat, Luminarch Aspirant and Ajani Steadfast all do roughly double work. Planeswalkers enter one loyalty higher and every plus ability gives one extra, so the Elspeths, Basri Ket and the Ajanis reach their ultimates a turn early. Nearly every game ends in combat. At bracket 4, Heliod, Sun-Crowned plus Walking Ballista is a backup infinite.

Game plan

  1. T1–2Mana rock or Land Tax, then a one- or two-drop that wants counters: Luminarch Aspirant, Ainok Bond-Kin, Esper Sentinel.
  2. T3Lae’zel. Put Swiftfoot Boots or Lightning Greaves on her as soon as you can: she is removed or countered in most games.
  3. T4–5An engine: Cathars' Crusade, Felidar Retreat or a planeswalker. Add Guild Artisan once Lae’zel can attack safely for Treasure.
  4. T6+Token makers into Crusade, a protection spell in hand, then swing with Ajani Unrelenting’s +1 or Akroma's Will.

What to watch for

  • Fast go-wide and aggro decks are the real problem. Against Jetmir, Fynn or Lathril, block early and hold Austere Command or Elspeth, Sun's Champion’s −3.
  • Hold Teferi's Protection, Flawless Maneuver or Unbreakable Formation until someone casts a wipe, not just until you’re ahead.
  • Never cast Walking Ballista for X=0 expecting Lae’zel to save it (see Rulings).

Win conditions

Elspeth, Sun's Champion{4}{W}{W}
Legendary Planeswalker Elspeth · Loyalty 4

[+1]: Create three 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens.

[-3]: Destroy all creatures with power 4 or greater.

[-7]: You get an emblem with "Creatures you control get +2/+2 and have flying."

Three Soldiers a turn into Cathars’ Crusade, then the +2/+2 flying emblem. With Lae’zel she enters on 5 loyalty, one turn closer to −7.

B4: cast in 657 games, won 64% (vs 36% without) · B3: cast in 685 games, won 61% (vs 34% without)
Ajani Unrelenting{4}{R}{R}
Legendary Planeswalker Ajani · Loyalty 5

Whenever you activate a loyalty ability, create a 2/2 colorless Wizard Soldier creature token named Cadet.

[+1]: Creatures you control get +1/+0 and gain haste until end of turn.

[-2]: Discard your hand, then draw a card for each creature you control.

[-3]: Ajani deals 4 damage to each creature except for tokens you control.

Every activation makes a Cadet. The +1 gives the team +1/+0 and haste, so a turn-6 Ajani usually means a lethal swing on turn 7.

B4: cast in 634 games, won 62% (vs 37% without) · B3: cast in 648 games, won 61% (vs 34% without)
Basri Ket{1}{W}{W}
Legendary Planeswalker Basri · Loyalty 3

[+1]: Put a +1/+1 counter on up to one target creature. It gains indestructible until end of turn.

[-2]: Whenever one or more nontoken creatures attack this turn, create that many 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens that are tapped and attacking.

[-6]: You get an emblem with "At the beginning of combat on your turn, create a 1/1 white Soldier creature token, then put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control."

With Lae’zel each +1 is +2, so the −6 emblem (a Soldier and a counter on everything every combat) comes online in two turns.

Rulings to know

Lae’zel and cards that enter with counters CR 122.6
Some spells and abilities refer to counters being put on an object. This refers to putting counters on that object while it's on the battlefield and also to an object that's given counters as it enters the battlefield.

Walking Ballista, Stonecoil Serpent, Mikaeus and Graft-style creatures all enter with one extra counter.

Planeswalkers enter with an extra loyalty CR 306.5b
A planeswalker has the intrinsic ability "This permanent enters with a number of loyalty counters on it equal to its printed loyalty number." This ability creates a replacement effect (see rule 614.1c).

Because entering loyalty counters are "put" on the walker (122.6), Lae’zel applies: Elspeth, Sun’s Champion starts on 5, Gideon on 5, Ajani Resolute on 3.

A Walking Ballista for X=0 still dies CR 704.5f
If a creature has toughness 0 or less, it's put into its owner's graveyard. Regeneration can't replace this event.

With X=0 no counters are being put on Ballista, so Lae’zel has nothing to add to. Cast it for at least X=1 (it then enters with 2).

Cathars’ Crusade with several creatures entering at once CR 603.2c
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.

Three Soldiers from Elspeth is three Crusade triggers, each putting two counters (with Lae’zel) on every creature.

Guild Artisan as your second commander CR 702.124k
"Choose a Background" means "You may designate two cards as your commander rather than one if one of them is this card and the other is a legendary Background enchantment card."

Guild Artisan starts in the command zone and only grants its ability to commander creatures, so it does nothing without Lae’zel on the battlefield.

Bracket 4 findings

  • 40.3% of games and 36.2% of series won across 1,800 random tables (fair share 25% / 16%). That's 2 points above the bracket 3 flex (38.3%), just outside the ±1.3 noise.
  • You lose to go-wide boards before yours comes together: Tokens / go-wide (32.1%), Typal (34.9%), Landfall (36.7%) and Aggro (37.8%) are the four worst rows, and you're knocked out first 41% of the time in those pods.
  • Lae'zel is the lightning rod: removed 2,819 times and countered 809 times over 4,368 games. Felidar Retreat, Basri Ket and the Ajanis keep winning without her (58–62% win when cast).
  • Heliod + Walking Ballista closed 54 kills (about 1 win in 30). The rest is combat: 4,751 combat kills and 411 by commander damage.

Bracket 3 findings

  • 38.3% of games and 33.3% of series won across 1,800 random tables, 2 points behind the bracket 4 list. The 4 swaps cost the combo kill and some speed.
  • Same weak spots: Tokens / go-wide (32.7%), Landfall (34.3%) and Aggro (35.2%). Fynn's poison and Jetmir's go-wide knock you out most.
  • The planeswalkers carry it: Ajani Unrelenting and Elspeth, Sun's Champion win 61% of the games they're cast in.
  • When Lae'zel never resolves you win 12% of games, so protect her: Swiftfoot Boots and Lightning Greaves on her are worth the mana.

How this was run

Each series is a random local-game-store table: three opponents from three different archetype categories, each an EDHREC average deck rolled at bracket 3 or 4, best of three. 100 series per category, 1,800 tables per version, run on the homelab on 4 October 2026.

The simulator is a rule-based AI with no table politics. For this deck it now models Lae’zel’s extra counter, planeswalker loyalty abilities and emblems for all eight walkers, Guild Artisan as a second commander, Cathars’ Crusade, Felidar Retreat, The Ozolith and the Heliod + Ballista loop. Treat small gaps as noise and big ones as direction, not exact numbers.
